```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(hpgR)
```

An allele's frequency changes when its copies contribute unequally to the
next generation. Each new copy samples one parental row with replacement.
`simulateForward()` carries out this simuPOP-derived copy-pool operation in R
and records every parental choice.

```{r copying}
initial <- matrix(c(rep(1L, 3), rep(0L, 7)), ncol = 1L)
record <- simulateForward(initial, sizes = c(5, 5, 3, 3, 5), seed = 8149L)
states <- replayCopying(initial, record$parents)
stopifnot(identical(states, record$states))
vapply(states, function(G) mean(G[, 1]), numeric(1L))
```

Here $N$ is the diploid population size and each matrix has $2N$ haploid rows.
`replayCopying()` reproduces every inherited allele using the recorded
parent choices.

This example isolates random copying. `simulatePopulation()` separately
models diploid reproduction with mutation, recombination and founder sampling.
